investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official 'Next events in the Grande salle Pierre Boulez' calendar page found NO event data server-rendered at all — only hidden form inputs and a loading spinner around an empty '#agenda-events' container. Level 2 STRUCTURAL: identified the platform as Drupal with its JSON:API module enabled, enumerated every JSON:API resource type (no event/concert/seance resource exists among them), then inspected the page's own publicly-referenced Drupal-aggregated JS bundles and found the actual client-side AJAX call target ('/{lang}/agenda-ajax') and its 'place_i' venue-filter query parameter, cross-referenced against the calendar page's own JSON:API node representation (field_agd_places: ['45']). Querying that discovered endpoint directly (plain curl, no browser) returned real, correctly-scoped event data, and each event's own detail-page link carried a complete schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://philharmoniedeparis.fr/en/calendar-selection/next-events-grande-salle-pierre-boulez returned a fully-formed page shell, but the actual event-list container is empty in the raw HTML (only hidden inputs like last_date/last_group/playlist and a spinner.gif) — the concert schedule is genuinely not present anywhere in the server-rendered response; it is injected by client-side JavaScript after page load.

Identified the platform as Drupal (drupal-settings-json script, pdp_theme). Queried the site's own public JSON:API entrypoint (/jsonapi) and enumerated every exposed resource type: no event/concert/seance/programme content-type resource exists among them, and the one node type this page itself is built from ('node--filtered_agenda', id 982) has an empty 'field_agd_events' relationship — the actual concert schedule is not modelled as a JSON:API-exposed entity at all. Inspected this page's own publicly-referenced Drupal-aggregated JS bundles (linked directly from the page's own <script src>) and found the real client-side AJAX call: callbackURL = '/' + lang + '/agenda-ajax', with a 'place_i' query parameter built from checked '.filter-places' checkboxes. Cross-referencing the SAME node's own JSON:API 'field_agd_places' value (['45']) as a reasoned candidate for this exact page's own place filter, then issuing a direct, single curl GET of https://philharmoniedeparis.fr/en/agenda-ajax?place_i=45, returned a JSON response whose own '.content' HTML fragment contains dozens of real EventCard entries, 60/60 sampled venue-name mentions reading exactly 'Grande salle Pierre Boulez - Philharmonie' — confirming the parameter value. Each EventCard's own detail-page link (/en/activite/{eventId}?itemId={performanceId}) was then fetched directly and found to carry one complete, well-formed schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block (title, full ISO start/end instants with explicit UTC offsets, venue name+address, and priced ticket offers) — fully answering the investigation question with no browser/headless observation needed at any point.

venue_reference: Philharmonie de Paris — Grande Salle Pierre Boulez, 221 Avenue Jean-Jaurès, 75019 Paris

identity.notes: The retained calendar page's own <title> reads 'Next events in the Grande salle Pierre Boulez | Philharmonie de Paris' at the venue's own domain philharmoniedeparis.fr. The detail page's own JSON-LD 'organizer' field directly states name 'Cité de la musique – Philharmonie de Paris', url 'https://philharmoniedeparis.fr', and a PostalAddress ('221, avenue Jean-Jaurès', 75019, Paris) matching the given venue address exactly; the same JSON-LD's own 'location' (MusicVenue) states name 'Grande salle Pierre Boulez - Philharmonie' with the identical street address.

site_classification.platform: Drupal (JSON:API module enabled, but no event/concert/seance content-type resource is exposed through it — the actual schedule is fetched client-side via a bespoke, non-JSON:API controller endpoint, '/{lang}/agenda-ajax', discovered via the site's own public Drupal-aggregated JS bundle rather than any documented API). That endpoint returns a JSON wrapper whose own '.content' field is an HTML fragment of EventCard entries, each carrying a stable numeric event/performance id pair (data-event-eid/data-performance-eid) and a Unix-epoch start timestamp (data-timestamp) directly as HTML attributes; each EventCard's own detail-page link then carries a complete, well-formed schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block.

title.notes: The detail page's own JSON-LD MusicEvent 'name' field, stated directly, cross-checked identical against the same event's own 'EventCard-title' text in the agenda-ajax response.

start_date.notes: The detail page's own JSON-LD MusicEvent 'startDate' field ('2026-08-30T19:00:00+02:00'), stated directly. Cross-checked against the SAME event's own 'data-timestamp' HTML attribute in the agenda-ajax response (1788109200 Unix epoch seconds), which converts to the identical instant (2026-08-30T17:00:00Z = 2026-08-30T19:00:00+02:00) — two independently-retained first-party representations agreeing exactly.

time.value: 19:00+02:00 (explicit UTC offset present on the source's own JSON-LD field)
time.notes: Same JSON-LD 'startDate' field as start_date — a full ISO 8601 instant with an explicit numeric UTC offset.

end.notes: The detail page's own JSON-LD MusicEvent 'endDate' field, stated directly as a full ISO 8601 instant with explicit UTC offset — a genuine performance-end instant (2h45 after the 19:00 start), unlike Tempodrom Berlin's own JSON-LD 'endDate' (which meant 'last calendar day of a possibly multi-day run').

venue_location.value: Grande salle Pierre Boulez - Philharmonie, 221 avenue Jean-Jaurès, 75019 Paris
venue_location.notes: The detail page's own JSON-LD MusicEvent 'location' (MusicVenue) field states both name and full street address directly, cross-checked identical against the agenda-ajax EventCard's own 'EventCard-place' text ('Grande salle Pierre Boulez - Philharmonie').

source_record_id.notes: The agenda-ajax EventCard's own '<article data-event-eid="30097" data-performance-eid="149058">' HTML attributes, stated directly. The performance-eid distinguishes this specific scheduled performance from other performances of the same production (data-event-eid), matching the same per-occurrence-identity judgement already established for theatre-de-la-ville-paris-01's own event_dates split.

event_url.notes: The agenda-ajax EventCard's own detail-page href ('/en/activite/30097?itemId=149058'), stated directly, resolved against the site's own known base origin.

price.notes: The detail page's own JSON-LD MusicEvent 'offers' array (4 Offer entries: 45.00/35.00/30.00/45.00 EUR across different availability/category tiers) directly states a price on its first entry. This investigation records the FIRST directly-stated offer price (matching the existing, unmodified ingestion/json-ld/observation-adapter.mjs's own offerPriceText() behaviour, reused unchanged for this source) rather than computing a min/max range, so the claimed value exactly matches what the recommended collector family actually produces.

blockers.description: This source's own real detail-page JSON-LD contains literal, unescaped C0 control characters (raw newlines) inside string values (observed inside the MusicEvent's own multi-paragraph 'description' field) — valid-LOOKING JSON-LD, but not valid per the JSON spec, so the EXISTING ingestion/json-ld/parse.mjs's extractJsonLdNodes() (which calls JSON.parse(raw) directly) silently fails to parse it (0 nodes extracted, not an error, since that function already tolerates per-block parse failures by design). The exact, minimal, backward-compatible fix needed in that SHARED module (not made here, per this project's convention that an investigation must not edit shared generic collector modules itself): before JSON.parse(raw), strip/replace characters in the U+0000-U+001F control range from `raw`. This is strictly additive — no currently-passing JSON-LD source in this repository is known to contain literal control characters inside its own JSON-LD, so no existing behaviour changes. Until that shared fix lands, ingestion/philharmonie-paris/discovery.mjs carries its OWN local sanitizing wrapper (sanitiseJsonLdControlCharacters()) that pre-cleans retained HTML before delegating to the UNMODIFIED shared extractEventNodes()/normaliseJsonLdEvent().

The 'place_i=45' query-parameter value for Grande Salle Pierre Boulez was established by cross-referencing this exact calendar page's own JSON:API 'field_agd_places' value against the query-parameter name discovered in the site's own JS bundle, then confirming empirically (60/60 sampled venue-name mentions in the response body read 'Grande salle Pierre Boulez - Philharmonie', 0 mismatches) — not from any documented site mapping. A future internal id change by the operator could silently break this without any public notice; worth monitoring in a live collector (e.g. asserting the returned venue-name text still matches on every run), not a blocker to activation.

reasons: identity.status PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (calendar page title, detail page's own JSON-LD organizer/location matching the given venue address exactly).

acquisition_class SPA_API_DISCOVERABLE, a resolved supported class, reached at Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) after Level 1 was genuinely retained as INSUFFICIENT (the calendar page's raw HTML server-renders no event data at all).
CONFIRMED public data paths retained for the discovered agenda-ajax endpoint (correctly scoped to this exact hall) and a detail page carrying complete JSON-LD.
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE, independently cross-checked between the JSON-LD detail page and the agenda-ajax EventCard's own Unix-epoch timestamp attribute.
source_record_id PROVEN via the site's own stable event-id/performance-id attribute pair, directly present on every EventCard.
end, venue_location, event_url, and price all additionally PROVEN — a genuinely complete field set from a single, well-formed schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block per event.

recommended_family JSON_LD, reusing TWO existing generic families unchanged (ingestion/html-link-discovery/'s extractLinksMatching() to discover detail links inside the agenda-ajax response's own HTML fragment, and ingestion/json-ld/'s extractEventNodes()/normaliseJsonLdEvent()/toObservation() to parse each detail page) behind one small, local, non-shared sanitisation step for this source's own literal-control-character JSON-LD — classified PARIS_EXISTING_FAMILY_WITH_SMALL_FIX (see collector_assessment.blockers for the exact shared-module fix this recommends, not made here).
No unresolved CRITICAL blocker (two MINOR notes recorded: the shared-parser control-character tolerance this source needs, and the empirically-confirmed-but-undocumented place_i mapping).
